Mateo —

Thanks for the SOW. We reviewed and have two major issues that block signature:

1) Liability cap: $100k is not acceptable for us given the nature of the data and the potential downstream clinical use cases. We require a $1,000,000 cap for the pilot.
2) Indemnity: the proposed indemnity is too narrow. We need a broader customer-favorable indemnity for regulatory claims and third-party data misuse during the pilot.

We also noted the data residency and retention terms are not explicit enough for our compliance team.

Please escalate — our procurement deadline for this quarter is June 30 and a timely decision would help.

Anna Keller
Head of Procurement

Forwarding AstraGen's response — procurement is pushing hard for a $1M cap and wider indemnity. Key commercials: 3-month pilot, projected ARR conversion if pilot successful ~ $150k ARR in year 1, strategic account in healthcare vertical with potential expansion into clinical product.

Redlines attached: AstraGen-SOW-redline-legal.pdf (their counsel annotated).

Ask: we need legal + exec guidance on whether to accept a higher liability cap for the pilot and whether we can agree to a broader indemnity carve. If we don't move, we risk losing their pilot and a meaningful chance at expansion.

Notes:
- Risk team flagged that a $1M cap would exceed our standard playbook and likely needs CEO or CRO sign-off.
- Offset possibility: request AstraGen add an insurance requirement (certificate, $1M per occurrence) and limit cap to pilot scope/timebox (3 months).

Happy to hop on a 15-min call to walk through.

—Mateo
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: AstraGen pilot SOW and pilot pricing (needs escalation)

Team —

Reviewed AstraGen's requested changes and their counsel's annotations. Summary and suggested compromise below. I attached a one-page risk memo and redline we would send to the customer if approved.

Summary of AstraGen asks: $1M liability cap; broader indemnity for regulatory claims; explicit data residency obligations.

Monica's recommended path (pilot-specific, requires exec sign-off):
1) Increase liability cap to $500,000 for the 3-month pilot only (reverts to $100k in full production).
2) Keep indemnity reciprocal and limited to IP infringement and third-party claims tied to breach of our agreement; carve out broad regulatory indemnity but offer collaboration on remediation and a defined remediation credit.
3) Require AstraGen to provide proof of insurance: $1M per occurrence + naming Redwood as additional insured for the pilot.
4) Add explicit data residency and retention language for pilot data (US-only) and delete open-ended retention clauses.

Commercial offsets to propose to customer if we take on the cap increase: 1) reduce pilot discount from 25% to 15%, or 2) require a minimum conversion commitment (e.g., expedited pricing if converted to production within 90 days).

Risk note: $500k for a 3-month pilot is still above standard and exposes Redwood to more risk, but the account is strategic. If you want to accept $1M instead we should escalate to CEO for final approval and consider contract insurance/escrow protections.

Please confirm that I should draft the response for exec review. If approved, we will route the final sign-off to Jonas for authorization.

Attachments: AstraGen-SOW-redline-legal.pdf; risk-memo-astragen-0626.pdf

—Monica Patel
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: AstraGen pilot SOW and pilot pricing (needs escalation)

Thanks for the thorough analysis. I agree with Monica's recommended path with the following executive-level clearance:

- Approve liability cap increase to $500,000 for the 3-month pilot only, provided we obtain the insurance certificate (minimum $1M per occurrence) and add a contractual obligation for AstraGen to cooperate on remediation and a limitation on consequential damages tied to pilot misuse.
- We will not accept a blanket regulatory indemnity. Offer remediation support and limited remediation credits instead.
- Require that the $500k cap reverts to our standard $100k for any follow-on production contract unless approved separately.
- Approve the commercial offset: reduce pilot discount to 15% (instead of 25%) or include a 90-day conversion price trigger — leave the choice to Mateo in negotiations.

Mateo: proceed to draft the customer response reflecting the compromise. Monica, send the redline incorporating the $500k pilot cap, insurance language, and data residency statements; Laura, please coordinate the deal push in HubSpot and flag the deal for the finance team to reflect the modified discount.

I'll sign the exec approval email for records. If anything changes materially from the customer, escalate back up.

Jonas Weber
